Motion prompts, free to copy

Prompts for the motion graphics you see in viral Reels and Shorts: slamming text, app UI demos, animated charts, particles and characters. Copy a prompt, paste it into Claude or ChatGPT, and you get a ready animation as a single web page you can screen record or drop into your edit.


      

      
Paste into Claude or ChatGPT. Open the HTML file it gives you in a browser, then screen record it, or ask for a different size, colors or text.

    

  






  
How to turn a prompt into a video

  
1. Copy a prompt and paste it into Claude or ChatGPT. 2. Save the reply as a file ending in .html and open it in your browser. 3. Record the screen (on a phone, use the built-in screen recorder; on a Mac, press Shift + Command + 5). 4. Trim it, add music, and add captions with Auto Captions. Change any words, colors or timing by asking the AI in plain English.






What are motion prompts?


A motion prompt is a detailed instruction you paste into an AI like Claude or ChatGPT. It writes a small web page that plays the animation, which you can screen record and use in Reels, Shorts, ads and presentations, without After Effects.


Tips for better results
  • Ask for changes in plain words: "make it 9:16", "use my brand colours #E5157A and #1F4D3A", "change the text to …".
  • Ask for a slower or faster version if the timing feels off.
  • Record at 60 fps for the smoothest result.





  
Questions

  
Are these prompts free to use commercially?
Yes. Every prompt and preview here was written and made by Creator Bench. Use them in client work, monetised videos and ads.

  
Which AI should I paste them into?
Any AI that writes code works. Claude gives the most polished motion; ChatGPT and Gemini work too. Ask for changes in plain words, like "make it 9:16" or "use my brand colors".

  
How often are new prompts added?
We add new prompts regularly, based on what's trending on Reels and Shorts.

  
Do I need to know coding?
No. You only copy the prompt, paste the reply into a file ending in .html, and open it in your browser.
